title: How to pick a mini golf course (there are a lot)

p: Visit Myrtle Beach says the first mini golf course here opened in 1930, and the habit never wore off. Its own Mini Golf Trail counts more than 30 distinct courses along the Grand Strand, and other guides count 50 or more depending on where they draw the line. Either way, you can play a different theme every night of a week-long trip and not repeat yourself.
That's a mixed blessing. When every block has a volcano or a pirate ship, it's hard to tell which ones are worth your evening. This page is meant to help with that.

sections.h: Start with the theme, then the neighborhood
p: Pirates are the safe bet for kids: Captain Hook's, Pirate's Watch, Shipwreck Island, Mutiny Bay and Black Pearl all lean on the same swashbuckling idea but look quite different once you're on the course. Dinosaur fans have Jurassic Golf in Myrtle Beach and the Professor Hacker's courses in North Myrtle Beach. Molten Mountain has the volcano, and the Aloha courses and Jungle Lagoon go for palms and waterfalls.

If you'd rather not drive far, pick by neighborhood. Central Myrtle Beach has the biggest cluster, so you can walk between courses from many oceanfront hotels. North Myrtle Beach has a second cluster along Highway 17 near Barefoot Landing. Surfside and Murrells Inlet have fewer courses, but Gilligan's Island Funland and Inlet Adventure are good for a quieter round.

sections.h: Small things that make a difference
list: Summer afternoons are hot, and some courses have much more shade than others. If the heat bothers you, play after dinner or choose a course with trees and covered stretches.
Many courses also have an arcade, snack bar or ice cream shop on site, which is useful with younger kids but means the bill can creep up.
Hours change with the season, and a few courses close for stretches in winter. Call or check the course's own page before you drive over.
Rain usually ends a round, and policies on rain checks differ from course to course. Ask at the counter before you start if the sky looks doubtful.
For a rainy day, look at the indoor options in our Family and indoor section, such as 810 Billiards and Bowling's haunted course.
